head: pr17646-r3
claim: As in Bash, the refusal is reported where it happens, on the standard error in effect there (after `f 2>/dev/null` nothing is printed, and `f 2>log` writes it into `log`), and a refused function call or eval abandons the rest of the command it is in (the next top-level command runs, with `$?` 1) rather than letting each of the 500 callers carry on as if one command had failed. If that standard error cannot be written (deep nesting under a low descriptor limit, below), the enclosing command reports the refusal instead, so it is not lost.
instrument: Its own addon built from this commit, run through `Shell.run` against Bash 5.2.21 on `f 2>/dev/null`, `f 2>file`, `eval "$e" 2>/dev/null` and `. "$AGAIN" 2>/dev/null`; and mutation M1, which drops the `return err;` after a failed `display_error` in `report_abandonment` (crates/vendor/brush-core/src/shell/io.rs).
nearby_question: Is a refusal kept off the outer output when the write to its redirected standard error succeeds? The claim asks whether it is reported on the standard error in effect whatever that standard error is, and M1 had shown the fallback fires on any failed write.

wrong_verdict.text:
# Verdict: **yes** — #17646 may leave draft at `4ef2e3be03ab`

No blockers. Everything the body claims that I checked, I reproduced; nothing I probed beyond it broke.

**Mutation proof it is load-bearing.** I removed the one `return err;` from `report_abandonment` in `shell/io.rs` and rebuilt: the descriptor test goes red **and so does `runaway_function_recursion_is_refused_and_the_session_survives`**, both with one output line where two are expected — the refusal disappears entirely. So under a 1,024 soft limit the fallback is not an exotic path, it is the normal one; the body understates how load-bearing it is.

6. **No test or corpus case covers a refusal raised by a builtin under a redirection.** I checked it by hand: `eval "$e" 2>/dev/null` and `. "$AGAIN" 2>/dev/null` print nothing and give `after=1`, and in a pipeline each reports once and the parent carries on. Correct, but only because I ran it.

refutations.text: 1. **An unwritable redirected stderr leaks the refusal to the outer output.** On the head, `FUNCNEST=3; f() { f; }; f 2>&-` returns status 1 and emits `error: f: maximum function nesting level exceeded (3)` through the outer `Shell.run` callback. Bash returns 1 with no output. `f 2>/dev/full`, `{ f 2>&-; } 2>&-`, and `exec 2>&-; f` do the same, at soft descriptor limits 1,024 and 65,536. Even `f 2>&- | /bin/cat; printf 'PARENT=%s\n' "$?"` prints a diagnostic Bash suppresses. The error occurs with *ample* free descriptors; it is not the intended descriptor-exhaustion fallback. In `crates/vendor/brush-core/src/shell/io.rs:105-114` at the reviewed head, `report_abandonment` returns the original error after **any** failed write. `Program::execute` later writes it to another stderr. Only a failure to duplicate a descriptor should permit that fallback; a deliberately closed or unwritable stream must not cause a report elsewhere. Reproduction receipts: `results-all.tar.gz` entries `fd-closed-65536-*`, `fd-full-65536-*`, `fd-allclosed-1024-*`, `fd-exec_closed-1024-*`; and `results-supplement/` entries `supp-unwritable-461-*` through `supp-unwritable-466-*`.

refutations.source: /home/sami/.omp/agent/sessions/-src-oh-my-pi/2026-10-19T03-32-08-771Z_01a15237-75c3-7321-befb-e6e1cc57a948/ClaudeReview17646r3.jsonl message 6adc7148, 2026-11-01T10:06:13Z, lines 7-13 (the clearing reviewer's own reproduction, /mnt/nvme/sami/cr17646r3/evidence/failwrite.txt)
refutations.text:
| script | this head | Bash 5.2.21 |
|---|---|---|
| `f 2>/dev/null; printf 'PARENT\n'` | nothing, exit 1 | nothing, exit 1 |
| `f 2>&-; printf 'PARENT\n'` | **`error: f: maximum function nesting level exceeded (3)`**, exit 1 | nothing, exit 1 |
| `f 2>/dev/full; printf 'PARENT\n'` | **the same refusal**, exit 1 | nothing, exit 1 |

`report_abandonment` treats **every** `display_error` failure as "this stderr could not be written, hand the refusal to an enclosing command". Mutation M1 proves that fallback is needed for descriptor exhaustion — but a closed descriptor and a full device are also write failures, so the refusal escapes past the user's own redirection. That is the exact defect this round fixed for `2>/dev/null`, surviving wherever the write *fails* instead of *succeeds*. The code needs to distinguish "the descriptor machinery ran out" from "the redirection rejected it"; today it distinguishes only "wrote" from "did not write".

diagnosis.text: I cleared this and should not have. I tested `2>/dev/null` and `2>file` — both redirections whose write **succeeds** — and generalised to "redirections honoured". My own mutation result was pointing straight at it: M1 showed the fallback fires on *any* write failure, and I treated that as evidence the fallback worked rather than asking what else fails to write. Finding 6 of my seven non-blocking findings is withdrawn and replaced by this blocker.
